issues.title: Common metadata/cache evaluation contract
issues.description:
## References
[Implementation roadmap](https://github.com/TomOrth/deltrove/blob/main/docs/implementation-roadmap.md) · [Metadata evaluation plan](https://github.com/TomOrth/deltrove/blob/main/docs/metadata-evaluation-plan.md)

## Objective
Under F3, define the common reproducible workload and measurement contract for the distributed-metadata and shared-cache evaluations. Reuse the fixture IDs, seeds, and artifacts already defined by F0/A01; extend them only with explicit named cases needed to compare metadata and cache behavior. Keep observed pilot facts separate from synthetic assumptions.

## Scope
- Inventory F0 fixture IDs and map each to repository count/shape, metadata operations, object sizes, concurrency, read/write mix, cache state, and expected correctness oracle.
- Define baseline configurations and equal aggregate fleet resource budgets (including cache servers, clients, database/object service, network and added nodes) for PostgreSQL, candidate database spikes, local process cache, shared cache, and disk-cache arms. Include cold/warm state, offered/accepted/rejected load, drain interval, p50/p95/p99, throughput, CPU/RSS, SQL/WAL/lock/pool metrics, cache hit/miss/eviction/fill behavior, bytes transferred, and origin load.
- Define deterministic fault controls and independent client acknowledgment ledgers with post-fault authoritative outcome/object reconciliation, including isolation/write-skew, stale generation, lost response, revocation, cache poisoning, origin slowdown/failure, and cold restart.
- Pin the schema for evidence records, seed/configuration capture, environment/topology, license/dependency inventory, raw artifact retention, and how unsupported or not-run cases are reported.

## Prerequisites
F1's real PostgreSQL and fault-harness spine is available. F0/A01 workload fixtures exist or their absence is explicitly recorded. Do not make A14 depend on F3 completion or on an S milestone.

## Non-goals
No production database/cache adapter, no changed F0 acceptance targets, no invented customer workload measurements, no replacement of existing fixture IDs, and no claim that snapshots or external object storage share a transaction with SQL.

## Deliverables
Proposed future path: `docs/evaluations/scaling-evaluation-contract.md`, with fixture mapping, workload/config schemas, commands, oracle definitions, pinned versions/licenses, raw evidence layout, and open gaps. Record changes to F0 fixtures as explicit additions with rationale.

## Verification and acceptance
A second operator can regenerate each selected workload from recorded seed and config and reproduce the arm definitions. Demonstrate that deliberately injected write skew or stale-generation publication is rejected by the oracle, and that poisoned/wrong-tenant cache bytes are rejected or never served. Show at least one intentionally perturbed workload/config yields a detectable metric/oracle difference so the contract is not merely restating identical implementations. Acceptance requires all required fields populated or explicitly marked unsupported/not-run with cause; no results are represented as already measured.

## Handoff
Report revision, exact commands and environment, F0 fixture IDs, raw logs/metrics, dependency and image versions, license/source links, failures, unsupported cases, and unresolved comparability risks. Recommend whether A15/A16 can run on the common contract without adding further shared semantics.

## Ownership and coordination
Own the proposed experimental files under `experiments/scaling/A14/` and the dated evidence directory named above (or `docs/evaluations/A14/` when no specific directory is named). A14 owns the shared evaluation contract; downstream agents consume it. Coordinate changes to shared F0/F1 fixtures, schema, oracle, public API or production adapters with the integrator before editing. Keep experimental engine/client dependencies isolated from the default installation. Use the roadmap handoff template; no planning document or unrun check counts as a passed experiment.

issues.title: Distributed SQL compatibility and isolation spike
issues.description:
## References
[Implementation roadmap](https://github.com/TomOrth/deltrove/blob/main/docs/implementation-roadmap.md) · [Metadata evaluation plan](https://github.com/TomOrth/deltrove/blob/main/docs/metadata-evaluation-plan.md) · [Technical plan](https://github.com/TomOrth/deltrove/blob/main/docs/technical-plan.md)

## Objective
Under F3, establish a bounded semantic compatibility gate for evaluating distributed SQL against Deltrove's existing PostgreSQL-owned domain contract. Decide which candidate transaction patterns preserve required publication, generation, idempotency, outbox, authorization, and fencing invariants, and where semantics or operational limits require deferral. This is foundation research; it does not add production multi-database support to the MVP.

## Scope
- Extract the concrete SQL/domain contract from the technical plan, F1 fixture, and F0 workload IDs. Enumerate short critical transactions, serializable retry behavior, uniqueness/foreign-key constraints, atomic outbox, expected generations, idempotency ledger, and single authoritative writer per migration stage.
- Run minimal compatibility probes against CockroachDB and TiDB using the exact versions/configurations named by the metadata evaluation plan. For TiDB, proceed only with a reviewed invariant-preserving guard/locking protocol that passes every adversarial schedule; if this proof is unavailable, record TiDB as rejected for authoritative domain metadata and do not send it to A17. Include concurrent conflicting mutations, write skew, retry/abort classification, unique constraints, transaction restarts, lost commit response/reconciliation, stale owner fencing, and migration/schema features used by the contract.
- State the isolation guarantees actually exercised. Snapshot isolation must not be labeled Serializable; for TiDB, explicitly verify the relevant configuration and behavior before it can pass the semantic gate.
- Define which engines/cases remain eligible for A17 and the exact pass/defer criteria; include dependency/version and license provenance.

## Prerequisites
A14 is accepted. F1's real PostgreSQL domain fixture is the reference behavior. Read `docs/technical-plan.md`, `docs/research/acid-workflow-boundaries.md`, and the evolving `docs/metadata-evaluation-plan.md` and `docs/research/distributed-metadata.md`.

## Non-goals
No production adapter, no engine migration, no geographic concurrent-write design, no claim of distributed ACID spanning SQL and S3-compatible object storage, and no broad database survey without executable probes tied to the current contract.

## Deliverables
The existing `docs/metadata-evaluation-plan.md` defines the proposed protocol/cases. Preserve source-backed research and write dated findings, scripts, raw evidence and recommendation to `docs/evaluations/A15-distributed-sql-semantics/`. Include a semantic matrix, minimal reproducible SQL/scripts, expected versus observed outcomes, engine/config/version/license pins, and explicit open gaps.

## Verification and acceptance
The same seeded concurrent cases run against PostgreSQL reference and each candidate actually exercised; retain raw SQL, config, logs, and outcome ledger. Include negative controls that intentionally permit write skew or remove fencing/unique protection and show the oracle catches the invariant violation. Demonstrate retry after a serialization/deadlock abort and reconciliation after a committed-but-lost response. Reject claims based solely on product documentation or snapshot-isolation nomenclature. Recommend `defer` if a required semantic cannot be demonstrated or support burden is unbounded.

## Handoff
Provide tested engine versions/configuration, exact commands and topology, SQL and raw outcome/fault artifacts, licenses/dependency provenance, semantic gaps, unsupported/not-run cases, and a concise gate result for A17. A pass means only that bounded capacity evaluation is eligible; it does not select or deploy an engine.

## Ownership and coordination
Own the proposed experimental files under `experiments/scaling/A15/` and the dated evidence directory named above (or `docs/evaluations/A15/` when no specific directory is named). A14 owns the shared evaluation contract; downstream agents consume it. Coordinate changes to shared F0/F1 fixtures, schema, oracle, public API or production adapters with the integrator before editing. Keep experimental engine/client dependencies isolated from the default installation. Use the roadmap handoff template; no planning document or unrun check counts as a passed experiment.

issues.title: Shared-cache qualification: shared, process-local, and disk baselines
issues.description:
## References
[Implementation roadmap](https://github.com/TomOrth/deltrove/blob/main/docs/implementation-roadmap.md) · [Cache evaluation plan](https://github.com/TomOrth/deltrove/blob/main/docs/cache-evaluation-plan.md) · [Shared-cache research](https://github.com/TomOrth/deltrove/blob/main/docs/research/shared-cache.md)

## Objective
Under S3, determine whether Deltrove benefits from a shared cache tier and record an adopt/defer/no-cache recommendation. Compare Moka plus Dragonfly and Moka plus Valkey against Moka alone under the same aggregate fleet resource envelope, and a disk-cache baseline for larger objects using A14 workloads. This card evaluates options; it does not require implementing a shared tier.

## Scope
- Reuse A14 workload IDs, warm/cold state, fleet and tenant mix, resource budgets, and metrics. Exercise metadata/read-through entries separately from immutable content-addressed objects; include object-size bands where a disk cache may be useful.
- Pin candidate versions, deployment configuration, client/library versions, licenses, hardware/topology, eviction/TTL policy, and cost assumptions. Compare origin bytes/requests, latency distributions, CPU/RSS, disk use and I/O, cache operations, fill concurrency, and recovery after restart or cache loss.
- Probe tenant/repository key isolation, authorization on every hit, policy/revocation behavior, wrong-key/digest corruption, poisoned entries, concurrent misses/single-flight, origin slowdown/failure, and bounded fill/stream resource use. Document that previously downloaded bytes cannot be recalled by later revocation.
- Recommend adopt, defer pending a trigger, or no shared cache; state measurable trigger/revisit conditions and what S3 implementation would separately need.

## Prerequisites
S2's independently scaled API/worker classes and resource budgets are available; A14's common workload and evidence schema is accepted. Read `docs/cache-evaluation-plan.md` and `docs/research/shared-cache.md` as they are prepared.

## Non-goals
No production cache rollout, no authority for cached authorization/ref/policy, no assumption that process-local Moka replaces persistent local storage or the workspace SQLite database, and no mandatory shared cache feature for release.

## Deliverables
Use `docs/cache-evaluation-plan.md` as the frozen protocol. Store dated results, raw metrics, and security/integrity findings in `docs/evaluations/A16-shared-cache/`; preserve `docs/research/shared-cache.md` as dated source-backed research. Preserve raw commands/config/logs and version/license pins.

## Verification and acceptance
Run comparable cold and warm workloads for each available arm under an equal aggregate fleet budget including cache server/client resources, database/object service and network; report extra-hardware arms separately. Deliberately test a cache miss storm, cache loss, origin delay/failure, wrong digest/tenant key, permission revocation between fill and hit, and slow/cancelled consumers. The correctness oracle must show that a cache hit never bypasses current authorization and corrupted content is rejected even when an attacker changes payload and its cache-stored checksum/input mapping; use independently trusted digests/mappings or an application authenticator, otherwise recompute from canonical data. Report failures and unsupported arms plainly; a mock-only arm cannot be reported as a measured product comparison. Decision states adoption criteria and S3 follow-up scope, or explicitly recommends defer/no shared tier.

## Handoff
Include exact fixture IDs/seeds, commands, topology, software/images and license sources, raw metrics/logs, cost model, resource limits, faults, limitations, and decision/revisit trigger. If adopted, describe a proposed next implementation card without silently treating this evaluation as implementation approval.

## Ownership and coordination
Own the proposed experimental files under `experiments/scaling/A16/` and the dated evidence directory named above (or `docs/evaluations/A16/` when no specific directory is named). A14 owns the shared evaluation contract; downstream agents consume it. Coordinate changes to shared F0/F1 fixtures, schema, oracle, public API or production adapters with the integrator before editing. Keep experimental engine/client dependencies isolated from the default installation. Use the roadmap handoff template; no planning document or unrun check counts as a passed experiment.

issues.title: Conditional distributed SQL capacity comparison
issues.description:
## References
[Implementation roadmap](https://github.com/TomOrth/deltrove/blob/main/docs/implementation-roadmap.md) · [Metadata evaluation plan](https://github.com/TomOrth/deltrove/blob/main/docs/metadata-evaluation-plan.md)

## Objective
Under S6, compare metadata capacity and operational behavior of tuned PostgreSQL/HA and repository-sharded PostgreSQL against CockroachDB, using A14's common workloads and A15's semantic gate. Include TiDB only if A15 demonstrated the required semantics for the exact tested configuration. Start this card only when S6 measurements hit the documented single-primary capacity trigger or a concrete multi-region requirement calls for evaluation; otherwise record `deferred: trigger not met` with evidence.

## Scope
- Keep correctness workload, logical operation mix, resource envelope, offered load, latency/SLO accounting, and object service fixed across arms. Compare optimized indexes/query plans/batching first; distinguish vertical/tuned primary, HA failover, repository-sharded PostgreSQL, and distributed SQL topologies. Do not imply repository sharding splits one repository's transaction authority.
- Exercise representative hot-repository ref serialization, graph/tree metadata, idempotency/outbox, concurrent writes, workflow transitions, mixed tenant fairness, failover/retry, backup/restore readiness, and connection/pool budgets including rollout surge.
- Capture capacity curves and p50/p95/p99, throughput, abort/retry rate, CPU/RSS, storage/WAL/replication, locks/queues, network, operational steps, licensing, and cost. Include cold start, steady state, overload and drain.
- Compare semantic gate outcomes and operational failure modes. State the explicit result: retain PostgreSQL/tune or shard by repository, defer distributed SQL, or propose a separately reviewed alternate-engine implementation and migration qualification.

## Prerequisites
S1 HA/durability and S2 API/worker scale qualification are available. A15 passes for any candidate included. A14 workload/evidence contract is accepted. The trigger is evidenced by S6 or a written multi-region requirement.

## Non-goals
No automatic database swap, production alternate-engine adapter, multi-engine support, cross-shard repository transactions, or claim that a database transaction makes external object storage atomic. A17/A18 do not gate the core release when deferred.

## Deliverables
Use the frozen `docs/metadata-evaluation-plan.md`. Store trigger evidence, compared topology/configuration, raw findings, semantic status, licenses, cost, recommendation, and unresolved migration risks in `docs/evaluations/A17-distributed-sql/`; preserve dated source-backed research.

## Verification and acceptance
Use pinned, reproducible topologies and same seeded workloads. Compare against PostgreSQL reference correctness under concurrency and fault cases; record raw conflict/retry/outcome ledgers. Negative controls must detect at least one deliberate isolation/ownership-fencing violation and one overload/resource-budget violation. Include failover and lost-response cases, and report unsupported/not-run arms without extrapolation. Acceptance requires the trigger, comparable capacity/correctness evidence, source/license pins, and a documented decision. If the trigger is absent, a decision-quality defer record is the accepted outcome.

## Handoff
State trigger and why it is met (or not), all engine/server/client versions, full config/topology, hardware, exact commands, raw metrics/logs, dataset IDs/seeds, license links, costs, faults, limitations, and whether A18 is required. Any implementation proposal returns for separate architecture and migration approval.

## Ownership and coordination
Own the proposed experimental files under `experiments/scaling/A17/` and the dated evidence directory named above (or `docs/evaluations/A17/` when no specific directory is named). A14 owns the shared evaluation contract; downstream agents consume it. Coordinate changes to shared F0/F1 fixtures, schema, oracle, public API or production adapters with the integrator before editing. Keep experimental engine/client dependencies isolated from the default installation. Use the roadmap handoff template; no planning document or unrun check counts as a passed experiment.

issues.title: Conditional selected-engine migration, restore, rollback, and epoch qualification
issues.description:
## References
[Implementation roadmap](https://github.com/TomOrth/deltrove/blob/main/docs/implementation-roadmap.md) · [Metadata evaluation plan](https://github.com/TomOrth/deltrove/blob/main/docs/metadata-evaluation-plan.md)

## Objective
If and only if A17 recommends and the maintainer separately selects a non-PostgreSQL engine for an experimental implementation path, qualify the proposed metadata migration, backup/restore, rollback boundaries, recovery epochs, and old-controller fencing before any production cutover is considered. If A17 retains PostgreSQL or defers, record `skipped: no alternate engine selected` and the reason; the skip is complete.

## Scope
- Define a migration/restore rehearsal over representative seeded repositories and domain/outbox/idempotency data, with schema-version and compatibility mapping. Identify the source of truth at each stage and the exact single-writer boundary.
- Rehearse snapshot/CDC or other explicitly selected transfer, consistency verification, cutover fencing, stale worker/callback rejection, recovery epoch allocation, restore with mismatched metadata/object recovery points, and rollback or forward-recovery limits. Keep object bytes external and test reachability/retention separately.
- Record downtime/lag, rejected or accepted mutation ledger, RPO/RTO observations, failure points, credentials/replica fencing, and operational prerequisites. Pin tools, versions, images, licenses, and checksums.

## Prerequisites
A17 has a documented alternate-engine recommendation and the maintainer has selected that path for further qualification. Read the accepted A17 evidence and `docs/research/distributed-metadata.md`. If no engine is selected, do not execute migration experiments.

## Non-goals
No automatic or in-place production migration, no generalized engine-neutral migration framework, no dual-writer period, no approval of deployment, and no promise of rollback after incompatible writes.

## Deliverables
Store rehearsal scripts/configuration, checksums, outcome ledger, explicit irreversible boundaries, and runbook draft in `docs/evaluations/A18-migration-qualification/`; keep the source-backed research document unchanged. Provide a go/no-go recommendation for a separately scoped implementation package.

## Verification and acceptance
Inject interruption during transfer, before cutover, after cutover, during restore, and during rollback/forward recovery. Prove the old authority is fenced and cannot publish; verify no acknowledged domain outcome disappears within the selected, explicitly declared failure and acknowledgment profile; do not relax its RPO to make migration pass. Verify objects reachable from restored metadata are present and digest-valid. Deliberately restore mismatched recovery points and stale epochs and show the oracle rejects publication. Acceptance requires repeatable rehearsal, explicit operator steps, bounded/declared loss and downtime, raw evidence and a named rollback boundary. When skipped, cite A17 and retain the skip record.

## Handoff
Provide selected engine/version and license pins, source/destination schema revisions, exact commands, configs, topology, checksums, raw fault logs and outcome ledger, recovery epoch evidence, limitations, irreversible steps, and operator review findings. Clearly mark the result as qualification evidence, not authorization to switch production.

## Ownership and coordination
Own the proposed experimental files under `experiments/scaling/A18/` and the dated evidence directory named above (or `docs/evaluations/A18/` when no specific directory is named). A14 owns the shared evaluation contract; downstream agents consume it. Coordinate changes to shared F0/F1 fixtures, schema, oracle, public API or production adapters with the integrator before editing. Keep experimental engine/client dependencies isolated from the default installation. Use the roadmap handoff template; no planning document or unrun check counts as a passed experiment.
